attrs.text: **Code-Mode dispatches merge by root-call context.** Inner calls carry no turn or step, so each root call opens its own context keyed by the root call id, and the builder merges its dispatches into the step that owns the runner. A window that lost the dispatch start still merges the calls but cannot show their measured duration.

title: **Known limitation: no whole-session wall projection.** The totals row substitutes model time + tool time because the host projections expose no whole-session wall clock. The tool segment sums paired call durations, so parallel calls can ma...

attrs.text: **Known limitation: no whole-session wall projection.** The totals row substitutes model time + tool time because the host projections expose no whole-session wall clock. The tool segment sums paired call durations, so parallel calls can make that split look longer than a non-overlapping wall interval. This is recorded here; the view does not change host logic to fill the gap.

attrs.text: **Recorded-session coverage is exempted for this experimental PR.** Package tests cover folding, aggregation, formatting, paging, and the jsdom table; `apps/web/tests/client-ui-stats-panel.e2e.ts` mounts the plugin through a test-only overlay over the shipped Web surface and compares a committed ARIA golden. By owner decision, this experimental PR does not add a keyless recorded-session scenario; a profile or bundle promotion must add one.

title: **Timing is derived, not sampled.** Total time is the last step's end minus the first step's start; queueing and scheduler waits land in the "rest" segment. The total-time bar draws tool calls as the union of their paired intervals, so para...

attrs.text: **Timing is derived, not sampled.** Total time is the last step's end minus the first step's start; queueing and scheduler waits land in the "rest" segment. The total-time bar draws tool calls as the union of their paired intervals, so parallel calls count once; the tool column keeps the summed per-call time. A turn bar is scaled against the turns currently visible on screen, so a much larger turn that scrolled away does not flatten the rows in view.

title: **Prompt images load through the shared image cache.** The pill and its preview resolve durable attachments with `uiConversation.imageUrl`, so the cache owns and revokes the browser URLs per Session binding; the view creates none of its own...

attrs.text: **Prompt images load through the shared image cache.** The pill and its preview resolve durable attachments with `uiConversation.imageUrl`, so the cache owns and revokes the browser URLs per Session binding; the view creates none of its own. A failed read shows a localized failure state with retry. Touch clients do not open the hover preview; tapping the pill loads the first image directly.

title: **Archive held in memory** — the whole upload stays in Host memory during the import, bounded by `maxUploadBytes`, plus one converted conversation, one image entry at a time, and the references of the images stored so far; one Host runs one...

attrs.text: **Archive held in memory** — the whole upload stays in Host memory during the import, bounded by `maxUploadBytes`, plus one converted conversation, one image entry at a time, and the references of the images stored so far; one Host runs one import at a time. Conversations and images the index does not select are never inflated.

title: **Synthetic file cards** — images the export lacks, of an unsupported type, over `maxEntryBytes`, or rejected by the attachment service (for example over its size limit), and every non-image file, become cards without bytes: they show the n...

attrs.text: **Synthetic file cards** — images the export lacks, of an unsupported type, over `maxEntryBytes`, or rejected by the attachment service (for example over its size limit), and every non-image file, become cards without bytes: they show the name and the exported size, cannot be opened, and name no stored object, so a model that reads the named path finds nothing. Non-image file bodies are not in the export.

title: **Images without a referencing event** — the image pass stores every image entry of a selected conversation before any conversation is parsed. Images of a withdrawn round, of a branch the import drops, and of a conversation whose conversion...

attrs.text: **Images without a referencing event** — the image pass stores every image entry of a selected conversation before any conversation is parsed. Images of a withdrawn round, of a branch the import drops, and of a conversation whose conversion or `Session.create` seed validation later fails stay as attachments that no event references. Neither `SessionPersistence` nor the attachment store offers a removal, so those bytes remain.

title: **Synchronous inflation** — the streaming pass inflates each selected entry synchronously with fflate's `UnzipInflate`. An entry that declares a small `originalSize` but carries highly compressed data keeps inflating until the entry ends, a...

attrs.text: **Synchronous inflation** — the streaming pass inflates each selected entry synchronously with fflate's `UnzipInflate`. An entry that declares a small `originalSize` but carries highly compressed data keeps inflating until the entry ends, and `maxEntryBytes` only stops those bytes being kept. A crafted archive can occupy the Host for a long time before the entry is rejected.

attrs.text: **Duplicate local file headers** — duplicate detection covers the central directory only. A second local file header renamed to an existing entry name is not detected, so an archive can deliver more conversations than the index lists, and the write count is not additionally guarded.

title: **`read()` truncates** — `ExportArchive.read` returns at most the size an entry declares, truncating one that inflates to more, while `stream` reports that condition as a size failure. The manifest, the index, and a replacement conversation...

attrs.text: **`read()` truncates** — `ExportArchive.read` returns at most the size an entry declares, truncating one that inflates to more, while `stream` reports that condition as a size failure. The manifest, the index, and a replacement conversation are read by name, so one of them can arrive truncated. Each by-name read also re-parses the whole central directory: the manifest and the index pay it once each, and a replacement conversation pays once more.
